'''Beth Alison Shapiro''' (born January 14, 1976)<ref name=MacArthur>{{cite web|title=2009 MacArthur Fellows: Beth Shapiro|url=https://www.macfound.org/site/c.lkLXJ8MQKrH/b.5458039/k.8CB8/Beth_Shapiro.htm|publisher=MacArthur Foundation|access-date=19 March 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307102911/https://www.macfound.org/fellows/64/|archive-date=2016-03-07|website=macfound.org|author=Anon|year=2011}}</ref> is an American [[Evolutionary biology|evolutionary]] [[Molecular biology|molecular]] [[biologist]], associate director for conservation genomics at the [[UC Santa Cruz Genomics Institute]], and a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] investigator.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Beth Shapiro, DPhil {{!}} Investigator Profile {{!}} 2018-Present |url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/beth-shapiro |access-date=2024-01-18 |website=www.hhmi.org |language=en}}</ref><ref name="None">{{cite news |title=Ancient DNA expert Beth Shapiro named CSO of Colossal |url=https://genomics.ucsc.edu/2024/03/20/beth-shapiro-cso-of-colossal/ |work=UC Santa Cruz}}</ref> She also teaches in the Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]].<ref name="None" />  In March 2024, Shapiro began a three year sabbatical to become the chief scientific officer of [[Colossal Biosciences]].<ref name="None" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Game of clones: Colossal's new wolves are cute, but are they dire? |url=https://www.technologyreview.com/2025/04/08/1114371/game-of-clones-colossals-new-wolves-are-cute-but-are-they-dire/ |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=MIT Technology Review |language=en}}</ref> 

Shapiro's work has centered on the analysis of [[ancient DNA]].<ref name="tedx">{{YouTube|title=Ancient DNA -- What It Is and What It Could Be: Beth Shapiro at TEDxDeExtinction|id=DajRM7VyeZ4}} [[TEDx]] talk</ref><ref name="googlescholar">{{Google Scholar id}}</ref> She was awarded a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]] in 2006<ref name=urf/> and a [[MacArthur Fellows Program|MacArthur Fellowship]] in 2009.<ref name="MacArthur" /><ref name="cv">{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314091702/https://homes.bio.psu.edu/people/faculty/bshapiro/ShapiroCV_101018.pdf|first=Beth|last=Shapiro|year=2012|title=Beth Shapiro Curriculum Vitae at Penn State University|archive-date=2012-03-14|url=https://homes.bio.psu.edu/people/faculty/bshapiro/ShapiroCV_101018.pdf}}</ref> She was elected a Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/news/2025-nas-election/|title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and International Members|website=www.nasonline.org|date=April 29, 2025|access-date=May 7, 2025}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
On January 14, 1976, Shapiro was born in [[Allentown, Pennsylvania]].<ref name=ResPnSt>{{cite web|last=Beattie-Moss|first=Melissa|title=Evolution of a Scientist: An Interview with Beth Shapiro|url=http://www.rps.psu.edu/profiles/shapiro.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722182908/http://www.rps.psu.edu/profiles/shapiro.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=22 July 2011|publisher=Research Penn State|access-date=19 March 2011}}</ref><ref name="CBEC">{{cite book |title=Contemporary Biographies in Environment & Conservation |publisher=Salem Press |year=2014 |isbn=978-1-61925-539-5 |pages=117–118}}</ref> She grew up in [[Rome, Georgia]], where she served as a local news presenter while attending [[Rome High School]].<ref name=Rhodes>{{cite web|last1=Williams|first1=Phil|last2=Hannon|first2=Sharron|title=The Rhodes to Oxford: Ecology student, Foundation Fellow Beth Shapiro becomes UGA's third Rhodes Scholar in four years|url=http://www.uga.edu/columns/990111/front2.html|publisher=University of Georgia|access-date=19 March 2011}}</ref> 

In 1994, Shapiro graduated from Rome High School with a [[Academic grading in the United States|GPA]] of 4.0, and entered the [[University of Georgia]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Brice |first=Plott |title=Rhodes scholar from UGA awed by what awaits |newspaper=The Atlanta Constitution |date=21 December 1998 |page=23}}</ref> She studied [[Mandarin Chinese]], [[Spanish (language)|Spanish]], [[English literature]], and [[geology]] prior to choosing [[ecology]] as her major.<ref name="CBEC"/>

In 1999, Shapiro graduated ''[[summa cum laude]]'' with [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] and [[Master of Arts|MA]] degrees in ecology.<ref name="CBEC"/><ref name=MacArthur /> The same year, she was awarded a [[Rhodes Scholarship]].<ref name=Rhodes />

In 2003, Shapiro completed a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Oxford]] for research on inferring evolutionary history and processes using ancient [[DNA]] supervised by [[Alan J. Cooper]].<ref name=dphil>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|title=Inferring evolutionary history and processes using ancient DNA|first=Beth Alison|last=Shapiro|date=2003|url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph015759573|website=bodleian.ox.ac.uk|oclc=56923402|location=Oxford}}{{dead link|date=July 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Career==

In 2004, Shapiro was appointed a [[Wellcome Trust|Wellcome Trust Research Fellow]] at the [[University of Oxford]]<ref name="macfound">{{cite web|url=https://www.macfound.org/fellows/class-of-2009/beth-shapiro|title='Beth Shapiro page on the MacArthur Foundation website.}}</ref> and director of the Henry Wellcome Biomolecules Centre at Oxford, a position she held until 2007. In 2006, she was awarded a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]].<ref name=urf/> While at the Biomolecules Centre, Shapiro carried out [[mitochondrial]] [[DNA]] analysis of the [[dodo]].<ref name=dodo/><ref name=Curry>{{cite web|last=Curry|first=Andrew|title=How to Make a Dodo: Biologist Beth Shapiro has figured out a recipe for success in the field of ancient DNA research|url=http://www.smithsonianmag.com/specialsections/innovators/shapiro.html|archive-url=https://arquivo.pt/wayback/20091014133850/http://www.smithsonianmag.com/specialsections/innovators/shapiro.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 October 2009|publisher=Smithsonian Magazine|access-date=19 March 2011}}</ref>

Shapiro's research on [[ecology]] has been published in journals<ref name=googlescholar/> including ''[[Molecular Biology and Evolution]]'',<ref name=Drummond2005/> ''[[PLOS Biology]]'',<ref name="PennyBunce2005">{{cite journal|last1=Penny|first1=David|last2=Bunce|first2=Michael|last3=Szulkin|first3=Marta|last4=Lerner|first4=Heather R L|last5=Barnes|first5=Ian|last6=Shapiro|first6=Beth|last7=Cooper|first7=Alan|last8=Holdaway|first8=Richard N|title=Ancient DNA Provides New Insights into the Evolutionary History of New Zealand's Extinct Giant Eagle|journal=PLOS Biology|volume=3|issue=1|year=2005|pages=e9|issn=1545-7885|doi=10.1371/journal.pbio.0030009|pmid=15660162 |pmc=539324 |doi-access=free }} {{open access}}</ref> ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'',<ref name=dodo/><ref name="Poinar2006">{{cite journal|last1=Poinar|first1=H. N.|title=Metagenomics to Paleogenomics: Large-Scale Sequencing of Mammoth DNA|journal=Science|volume=311|issue=5759|year=2006|pages=392–394|issn=0036-8075|doi=10.1126/science.1123360|pmid=16368896|bibcode=2006Sci...311..392P|s2cid=11238470}} {{subscription required}}</ref><ref name=Shapiro2004/> and ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]''.<ref name="LorenzenNogués-Bravo2011">{{cite journal|last1=Lorenzen|first1=Eline D.|last2=Nogués-Bravo|first2=David|last3=Orlando|first3=Ludovic|last4=Weinstock|first4=Jaco|last5=Binladen|first5=Jonas|last6=Marske|first6=Katharine A.|last7=Ugan|first7=Andrew|last8=Borregaard|first8=Michael K.|last9=Gilbert|first9=M. In 2024, Shapiro was appointed as chief science officer of [[Colossal Biosciences]] to help the company meet its [[de-extinction]] and [[wildlife conservation|species preservation]] goals.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.siliconhillsnews.com/2024/03/19/colossal-hires-ancient-dna-expert-beth-shapiro-as-chief-science-officer/|author=Laura Lorek|date=March 19, 2024|title=Colossal Hires Ancient DNA Expert Beth Shapiro as Chief Science Officer|work=Silicon Hills News}}</ref> In the same year, Shapiro received backlash and become a target of [[fan activism]] and [[Troll (slang)|trolling]] from fans of the ''[[Jurassic Park (franchise)|Jurassic Park]]'' media franchise for stating dinosaur de-extinction is impossible, or at least not possible in the way it is commonly depicted in [[science fiction]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shuyi |first=Lee |date=2024-09-11 |title=Dinosaurs' return deemed impossible by scientist |url=https://thethaiger.com/world/news/604869/ |access-date=2024-09-26 |website=Thaiger World |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/shorts/q79z0gUMsoc |title=Me, the social media manager, when people get mad at Dr. Beth Shapiro in the comments |language=en |access-date=2024-09-26 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref> 

In 2025, Colossal announced that they had created [[woolly mouse|woolly mice]] as part of the process of bringing back [[mammoth]]s. When this was dismissed by philosopher [[Craig Callender]] as "a stunt", Shapiro replied, "Some people argue that our whole company is a stunt{{nbsp}}... Gene editing could be used to help species become resistant to disease, to restore missing genetic variation or to correct gene sequences that lead to genetic disease but have become fixed in that population."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Popescu |first=Adam |date=4 March 2025 |title=Company Seeking to Resurrect the Woolly Mammoth Creates a 'Woolly Mouse' |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/company-seeking-to-resurrect-the-woolly-mammoth-creates-a-woolly-mouse/ |access-date=2025-03-06 |website=Scientific American |language=en}}</ref>

In 2025, Colossal claimed that it had resurrected the [[dire wolf]] which was disputed by the science community.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Game of clones: Colossal's new wolves are cute, but are they dire? |url=https://www.technologyreview.com/2025/04/08/1114371/game-of-clones-colossals-new-wolves-are-cute-but-are-they-dire/ |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=MIT Technology Review |language=en}}</ref> As part of the project, Colossal also said it cloned several [[Red wolf|red wolves]], an American species of wolves considered to be one of the most endangered wolves in the world.<ref name=":1" /> Shapiro said they hoped the rebirth of the dire wolves would bring attention and get people excited over the idea of using biotechnology to support conservation efforts.<ref name=":1" />

She is an elected member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2025/04/beth-shapiro-elected-nas/|title=Acclaimed evolutionary biologist Beth Shapiro elected to National Academy of Sciences|date=30 April 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life ==
Shapiro is married to [[biomolecular engineering]] professor Richard Edward Green and has two sons.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Sarah C. P.|date=2022 |title=If genes could talk |url=https://inquiry.ucsc.edu/2022-23/if-genes-could-talk/ |website=inquiry.ucsc.edu |publisher=Regents of the University of California |access-date=26 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Beattie-Moss |first1=Melissa|date=August 30, 2010 |title=Evolution of a Scientist |url=https://www.psu.edu/news/research/story/evolution-scientist |website=psu.edu |publisher=The Pennsylvania State University |access-date=26 September 2025}}</ref>
